chapter: Depression years and New Orleans trumpeters
title: Jules Baduc's band and Doc Rando
summary: Jules Baduc played banjo and led a band at the Little Club; Henry Rando sang, and Doc Rando went on from medicine or dentistry to play with Crosby and serve on a union board.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Jules Badouk played, he played banjo. And he had a very, very fine band. They played in the Little Club. That was many years ago. Had a very fine bunch of boys in that outfit. And of course, Ray played with him too. I think Monk played with him a whole lot. Yeah, Monk played with him there. But Jules was a very fine person. There was a young fellow by the name of Henry. Rando used to sing, very fine, very fine singer. He used to sing with him. Then Doc Rando, you know, he's... I think, did he graduate from Tulane? I don't remember whether he graduated from Tulane as a doctor of medicine or whether it was Loyola in dentistry. But he went right on playing music.
He just didn't care about it.

Well, I guess he cared about it, but he achieved the knowledge that he was after. But as far as practicing part, I don't know just how long he practiced. But he never did quit playing music. And he just went on and off playing music. In fact, Doc played with Crosby's band. And today, I think that he's one of the board of directors of Local 47 in Los Angeles. He was on the board. Anyway, whether he still is, I don't know. He may be in his profession out there now.
